concepts.def: Affluent residents replacing working-class in inner cities; rising rents displace original communities.
Unplanned housing without legal tenure; 1 billion people worldwide live in slums.
Poverty, poor housing, low education reinforcing intergenerational disadvantage.
Concentration of students changing demographics; e.g. Leeds, Nottingham areas.
Spatial separation by income, ethnicity or class.
Composite measure (IMD UK) covering income, employment, health, education.

walkthroughs.body_html: Shoreditch transformed since 2000: average house price rose from £150000 to £900000+. Original Bengali community displaced. Hackney gentrification linked to creative industries and Crossrail. Critics cite loss of affordable housing and community character.

Dharavi (Mumbai) houses 700000 people in 2.1 km^2 (density >330000/km^2). Generates $1 billion/yr from recycling, leather, pottery. Redevelopment plans (2022) propose rehousing residents in formal high-rise but raise concerns about livelihood loss.

Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD 2019) ranks LSOAs. Most deprived areas concentrate in north-east England, Liverpool, Birmingham inner city. Gap in life expectancy: 9.5 years between richest and poorest London boroughs (Kensington vs Tower Hamlets).
